reviews.comment: Dr. Mahapatra's lectures are heavily conceptual + he almost never works out numerical problems. Very passionate about student success and understanding. Will stay on a question until he's sure you understand it + know why/how the concept works. Syllabus implies you have to get iClicker qs right to get full credit, but you just have to answer them.
He cares alot about every student in the giant classroom. Though his 8 am's require iclicker he gives great feedback and experiments within the class.

Really likes to do physics demonstrations, which can be too much. I would rather just run practice problems. Likes to derive equations which doesn't really help for the tests. Office hours are helpful and recitation is really helpful.

I genuinely don't know why Professor Mahapatra has bad ratings. He's chill, encourages questions, and really wants students to understand. Mechanics requires lots of independent study and homework. He uses visual demos to keep class engaging. Participate, ask questions, attend (iClicker is graded), and you'll be fine.
Simply put he is just rude to you and the whole class. Belittles you for no reason and grades on a whim.

I don't get the hate. PHYS 206 is just straight up a hard course. He often gets confused as a mean professor because of his speeches, but at the end of the day it's because he cares. He made me realize that if I didn't focus up, I would not end up with the major I wanted, and while that sucks, everyone who entered engineering knew that walking in..

Lectures are disorganized. He has not prepared and does know prereqs. Slides are long, not organized. Lectures by clicking between 25+ slides with blurry, small diagrams. Disregarded syllabus: more labs than stated, changed grading criteria midway. Changed lab procedure midway into lab. Belittles and speaks down on others, students and faculty.

Completely disregarded the syllabus. Added labs on a whim as the year progressed, and held an in-class quiz labeled as homework. Didn't come prepared to class (he didn't even know what the prereqs for the class were), and when he did teach, it was loaded with frequent insults to the intelligence of students and TAMU as a school.

Made more labs than the syllabus assigned, with more parts given to labs. Definition of "homework" was stretched to include an in-class quiz. i-Clicker is location based. Verbally belittles and disrespects his students, as well as his poor daughter. Constantly fought other students in class, told us he thought we were dumb hicks lol. Easy A tho.

Constantly degrades students during class, indicating a lack of respect for others' intelligence and the quality of the physics program at Texas A&M. He is reworking the circuits course this semester, and does not give clear grading or instructions, writing and posting labs minutes before class. Lack of planning hurts course quality significantly.
I didn't have an easy time in this class. Although I got a good grade- this teacher was not kind. Would always get mad when I asked a question. I do not recommend.

Mahapatra is caring and wants the best for his students. He will try to engage the class, and he makes obvious that his goal is to make sure each and every one understands the material. The pacing of the course is what makes it challenging, you will go beyond units that won't be on your next test, learn it or fall behind. The final gave out As.

206 UP prof - Very strict, one of the few profs who makes iclicker an actual grade, gets mad at people for asking a question, what he teaches doesn't relate to the exams AT ALL. Read textbook 2x to keep up, acc do hw(best way to learn) watch alot of organic chem tutor vids. TAKE UP THO, FREE A+ BC OF EZ FINAL. 206 is js hard - DEF take Kaya Ali!!!

PHYS206 itself is super hard, but Mahapatra is good at explaining all the concepts and formulas you need to solve problems. He actively seeks participation and hates when the class is lost, so ask questions and study your ass off for the exams, and you'll do good. Homeworks are very hard/long but they prepare you super well for the test so do them.
He knows what he's doing, you have to show up and actually try to learn because he teaches pretty well. It's a hard class, but the final exam is fairly simple and can save your grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mahapatra is honestly such a fair and good prof. He may seem stern or condescending but he honestly just wants the best for every student in his class. He genuinely cares so much about every student and will help you no matter what. He provides helpful demonstrations in class and explains each topic carefully and thoroughly. GO TO LEC AND LISTEN

Very strict, will call you out for talking or not knowing information if you ask a question. Also, the lectures are very hard to understand, it is basically a self taught course which would be fine if attendance was not mandatory due to iclicker. If you don't know physics, I would recommend taking a different prof. He is very scary.

This guy is like Yoda or Master Oogway, he is very wise, but it takes time before he reveals the answer. In office hours you gotta try hard to get the information outta of him, but I know he cares and puts effort in for his students. I would take him again though he explains pretty good.

TAKE UNIVERSITY for Physics. Don't Panic is TERRIBLE for Phys 206. The material is boring and he isn't too good of a prof but he does some cool demos and the grading for University Physics is so generous. If there are 5 answer choices you could basically get half or more points for all of them.

I don't recommend taking his class if you are new to Newtonian Physics. He treats the entire class as a review instead of teaching the material. One thing I also didn't like was how he didn't create an inviting environment for asking questions, in his eyes there were such things as "stupid questions". His office hours were hardly helpful.

My highschool did not have a physics class so I went in knowing nothing. Mahapatra's lectures were good, but at times he went over stuff fast making it difficult to understand. I often times left the lectures being very confused, but the homework and past exams are great for studying. He is also very strict but just doesn't want distractions.

He does his best teaching but I just couldn't learn from him. I was better off self-learning. He teaches concepts more than problem solving, & I think learning by exmpls is v imp to do well. He can be condescending. Class is hard if you dont have a good phys foundation. No idea why people like him so much, his teaching is mid. Just use youtube.

It's obvious that he cares, but I don't think he was all that good. He wasn't engaging but he tried his best. I wouldn't take him again. I've heard he accuses a lot of people cheating during exams for simply looking up. Keep your head down during exams.

He knows exactly what he's talking about in lectures and what students often get tripped upon. Pay attention in class because many niche topics were on the test. My only complaint was that he was a little intense and gives off a strict but caring dad vibe. Will make you feel bad if you are even whispering in class. Very good lecturer, though.
Lectures are not helpful whatsoever. Could not learn anything in lecture and had to learn all of it by myself.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rigorous teacher that REALLY wants the class to know the material. He lectures well. However, he isn't very accessible outside of class - he will outright just not respond to emails at times. I found my TA more helpful when I had questions about the material/exams. Homework is a pain to do.

I could tell he cared about his students, but unfortunately he just didn't help me learn. Lectures were hard to follow, I almost felt like I was learning Don't Panic physics and then going home and doing University work. Even used outside tutoring and got a B. If you're strong at physics, you'll be okay, but if you're not like me, try another prof.
Quite condescending. He makes you feel bad for asking questions. But other than that, he was better than most teachers. Uni physics has a better grading scheme than don't panic.

Dr. Mahapatra makes University 206 quite simple and easy, and he is funny and his class if full of demonstrations. 80% of the grade is centered around Learning Objective based exams, where making an A does not require too much work. Going to recitation is kind of annoying because the problems are excessively difficult compared homework or tests.

Great Professor. Honestly University Physics is extremally forgiving. It is very possible to make a 100/100 in this class if you actually do the homework and dont cheat. However recitation was an absolute joke; they gave hard absolutely useless problems that nobody did.

Professor Mahapatra is a great University Physics professor and I would definitely recommend taking him.  He is a funny lecturer and does a good job explaining physics concepts.  The class is 80% test based with 3 unit exams and a comprehensive exam at the end of the semester.

I think Professor Mahapatra is one of the better profs of University 206. His lectures are easy to follow and he uses iclickers in class to gauge how fast to go and take attendance. Just go to lecture and take a few practice exams before the real ones and you'll be fine
He was a good prof, not amazing. If you took physics in high school then it will be a breeze. iClickers were very annoying, but the exams were pretty easy and they're fairly easy.
Definitely one of the better professors for 206 and he actually wants his students to succeed. The tests can be kind of variable though; they can be a breeze or leave you questioning your life.

All the experiments he tries to do end up failing and that is the fun part about the class. The i-clickers are annoying and the lectures are mediocre. Overall, if you understand physics, then you can chill in his class. Else, you are ded. :|

He's actually a pretty good professor. He is incredibly knowledgeable in physics. The prelectures are annoying and can be kind of confusing but I thought he did a pretty good job of clearing up question s during lecture. Can come off a little rude sometimes but he clearly wants us to do well and wants us to master the content, not just memorize.

Rupak is def a tough love professor. He seems kind of harsh, but he just wants you to genuinely learn. Most of the bad reviews on here come from his harshness and not his teaching ability. His exam averages tended to be the highest among all the physics professors. He tries to teach for mastery as opposed to strict memorization.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, has great potential to be an awesome professor but rather comes across as condescending when someone would ask a simple question. Rather than answering it in a straight forward manner, he would suggest to the students to be more focused the next time so we don't ask such questions.

Honestly, you are fully capable of making an A in this class. Professor Mahapatra's lectures can be confusing at times, the reason is you actually have to come prepared to understand what is going on. At first, I was expecting a D or C in the class, but I came across Spartan Tutoring on youtube, it is tailored specifically for PHYS206, USE IT.

He's really intelligent on the subject matter and cares a lot about student comprehension. The exam problems are very similar to homework and lecture problems, and the he always provides good review material. The only issue is that he is limited in lecture time, so he usually covers the fundamentals and the homework covers more complex problems.

Rupak receives a lot of flak, but I think this is just because this is already a hard class in general. He probably the most intelligent professor I have had so far. He takes focus in class very seriously, but does joke sometimes. Somewhat of an accent. He really is a good guy, he might just get on to you for talking in class when he is lecturing.

Terrible Guy. Stay Away. He only cares about $3 million dark matter research. If he has to give you a makeup he will start lying to you in order to save time out of his schedule. Does not care about his students; he only cares about his research. I would suggest taking literally anyone else.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Excellent teacher who is probably one of the smartest and most knowledgeable professors on campus. Is involved with a cool dark matter project, yet despite that is able to effectively communicate and teach the students about physics. The tests for these classes can be an absolute cake walk or be 2 hours of torture. Clicker questions could be better
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Mahapatra knows what he's talking about and can explain it in way that students can understand. He moves a bit fast, and the concepts take a while to solidfy, so THE TEXTBOOK IS YOUR BEST FRIEND! Helpful in office hours. Accent is not a problem, but sit near the front and participate! He's passionate about physics, so show him that you care!
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly, he isn't as bad as people make him, but he is a big cry baby about people not participating in class. Also his attitude towards clicker questions make me dislike him more.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's really good about making sure you understand what's going on. He's patient and really wants you to understand physics and is always accessible to students. He writes questions based off of the past common exams; make sure to come to class! He remembers who does and is more open to bumping them up to an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Horrid. The iClickers are used for two purposes: to force people to attend lecture (which has been otherwise obviated by the required prelectures) and to torture you. It doesn't exactly take an MEd to tell that your first chance to try a concept should not be in a trick question every time without fail. Too much homework, even during Spring Break.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Not as bad as many people make him out to be. His lectures made sense and I enjoyed him well enough as a professor. It seems like most of the people that complained about his teaching style did not do all the required homework and reading, if you do those you will be fine.

People in my class complained that he didnt answer emails or that he was rude, but I never saw that side of him. I was a struggling physics student who went to his office hours twice and he was very helpful. He definitely cared if you passed or not, you just had to show up to class and show him respect and hell do the same for you. Id recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Rupaks lectures are pointless now because of flipIt Physics (pre-lecture system). Only reason to attend is clicker quizzes, says he wants 80% correct, and if no one participates, he will lie to students saying they are correct to get them to talk, then tell them they are wrong and never explain the right answer. Would avoid this prof if possible
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Rupak, is a very hard teacher and phys 218 is a very hard class. This class is designed to weed people out of engineer and Rupak does nothing to help. I learned nothing from lecture, but the lecture is mandatory because of the clicker questions. I learned everything from A+ or the textbook. His lecture slides are completely worthless.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Mahapatra is very knowledgeable about physics and his lectures are very clear and easy to follow. When he explains a concept, he does not move on until 80% of the students understand it (through clicker questions). He wants everyone to know what is going on and figure out how to tackle any kind of physics problem.
do not take him I repeat do not take him
average prof, awful person
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: awful prof, rude, and doesn't care if you are not smart

take him if you have to, just saying he is not good prof , all those other comments saying he cares are lies, he is rude, doesn't care if you are not smart and very inpatient, I would not recommend him. I repeat do not believe those other comments saying good things about him.

Horrific prof, goes way to fast, only cares about the the smart people, not accessible out of class, and when you meet him he is rude , he wont explain it to you and he is very inpatient , take hi if you have to, over all horrific person, average professor less than average I would say.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He isn't the best at explaining things. You will need to read the book and it helps to go to the SI sessions. You need to go to class for the clickers cuz there are a lot. Very good at explaining the concept but goes very fast in solving problems.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Mahapatra as a professor is aggressively average. However, one of the biggest issues he seemed to have was that he had a hard time empathizing with students and putting himself in their shoes. He didn't seem to know what we didn't understand and why we didn't understand it. Even when he would ask for feedback, his answers were often pointed.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Instead of commenting about how he is as a person like many of these people have already commented about, I want to talk about how he teaches. I honestly believe he is a great professor when it comes to teaching the material. He will stop and thoroughly explain concepts that might seem too difficult to understand at first.

When he reviews things we don't understand he doesn't actually tell us how to do it, he just repeats himself. He also is very hard to talk to outside of class-he won't help you if he doesn't think you payed him 100% attention (even if you did), and his help isn't helpful. In class he will do very simple examples, and exams are very complex.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I tried to participate in class, but he never called on me or answered my questions. He never answered my emails, save for one time where he was extremely rude in saying that I did not put enough effort into contacting him and lied about certain occasions. Basically he made me feel like I was stupid. While there are worse profs, I can't recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: 218 is hard but he helps you through it. I would recommend him over any of the other 218 professors.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Mahapatra is probably one of the best professors you can get for 218. I took the course on campus w/ him over the summer and he was so much better at explaining concepts than Eusebi was. He provided supplemental problems for every chapter which made great preperation for the tests and HW. Only weakness is that it he was hard to contact after class

Yes, Phys-218 is a hard class, but yes you can also get an A in the class. Rupak Mahapatra is a GREAT professor and genuinely cares about how his students are performing. If you read the chapter before going to lecture Phys-218 will be much easier as Mahapatra does a great job of filling in the gaps and preparing students for the exams. Take him!!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Physics is a hard class but taking it with Rupak made it a whole lot easier. He explains physics in a way that makes sense, and that definitely helped as our class's average was higher than most of the other sections. There's a lot of homework and takes forever to do so I didn't do it, which I got by just fine without it. Don't miss a flipit though

I would have dropped this course if it were not for Dr. Mahapatra, the materials were definitely not easily to understand, but Dr. Mahapatra was willing to explain it to students IF AND ONLY IF you ask and willing to spend your time to study hard for the test.  Be prepared to do a lot more extra study besides your homework and lectures.
Physics 218 is an all-around difficult choice, but he makes it easier. He is always willing to see you outside of class and he even encourages people to come to his office hours.

Rupak truly cared about the students' learning. In a lecture hall of 100+ students, he would stop for questions, and would answers any questions thoroughly. Lectures were very informative and interesting, and he kept the students engaged. Good mix of humor and seriousness. Always willing to help students outside of class. I recommend him to anyone.

Mahapatra is the nicest professot/teacher i have ever had in my life. Not only is he a great teacher, but he wil go through great lengths to help you succeed. That said, this is not an easy class. It is one of the hardest classes you will ever take at A&M, which is why you have to work really hard to succeed and Rupak can help you do that.

Mechanical physics is not easy, but Mahapatra is the best way to go. He is the leader of the top research in the world at the moment, the study and search for dark matter. In other words, he is a genius, which sometimes makes him go a little fast. He ALWAYS answers questions though and always holds office hours. NEVER skip SmartPhysics pre lecture.

For physics he makes his own test, and it can be hard to predict what is on the test. Over all if you study and do ALOT of practice problems you should pass. He does curve, but don't expect much. He can loose some students when he explains, but a good teacher to expose you to the over all topics.
